summary: Created an 11-phase plan to route every specs/state.json writer through one new mutex-guarded helper, agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/state-write.sh. Phases 1-3 build the helper, add task-lock.sh cmd_release ownership verification, and build an isolated-temp-root concurrency suite; phases 4-9 convert all nine writers plus both inline command-file writes in lowest-risk-first order; phase 10 makes the workflow-active marker per-session as a declared atomic batch; phase 11 handles the known extension-loader deploy gap, the zero-remaining-hand-rolled-sequences audit, and the convention docs. All edits target the source store, never .claude/**.
decisions_made: state-write.sh is a standalone invocable script, not a sourced function, matching the dominant convention for single-purpose state mutation and callable from both shell scripts and markdown bash blocks.

The helper's interface is an arbitrary jq filter plus --arg/--argjson passthrough, because the three real caller transform shapes (single-task field update, top-level array mutation, $cands-scoped bulk |=) cannot be expressed by a narrow task_number+field API.
Mutex acquire is fail-closed on timeout, adopting task-lock.sh's cmd_scope_acquire return-2 precedent; the two existing callers' WARNING-and-proceed fallback is removed, not preserved as an option.
skill-base.sh's two orphaned uncalled write functions are deleted rather than converted; only orchestrator-postflight.sh's live inline duplicates of that logic are converted.
cmd_release's ownership check is WARN-and-no-op, always return 0, mirroring cmd_scope_release exactly rather than force-refusing.
The workflow-active writer and all three consumers are one atomic-batch phase; a partial conversion reintroduces the hazard.
The extension-loader deploy gap is worked around with an explicit manual copy phase and recorded as still open, not fixed by this plan.
